title: Israeli Security Cabinet Reportedly Orders Readiness for Possible Iran Strike
dek: KAN reports Israel’s security cabinet ordered the military to step up readiness for a possible attack on Iran, as Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot urged Netanyahu to hold off until a new government forms.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The front of the Knesset, Israel’s parliament, in Jerusalem

keyPoints: KAN reported that Israel’s security cabinet had instructed the military on Wednesday to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Anadolu reported.
Gadi Eisenkot wrote to Netanyahu that he heads a transitional government that "no longer enjoys the confidence of the Knesset," and urged him not to launch unnecessary operations.
Netanyahu’s office called the letter "an irresponsible move and an overt attempt to politicize security issues."
The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance is considering face-to-face talks with Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei. Rezaei has denied negotiations are under way.
Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned that if the U.S. launches another war, every military base involved “from West Asia to Europe” would be a legitimate target, Al Jazeera reported.
body:
Israel's security cabinet has reportedly instructed the military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israel's public broadcaster KAN reported Thursday. The reported directive came as Gadi Eisenkot, the lawmaker tasked with forming the next government, urged caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to refrain from unnecessary military operations until a new government is in place, [Anadolu reported](https://aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israeli-security-cabinet-orders-military-to-prepare-for-possible-attack-on-iran-report/4121434).

## The cabinet directive

KAN said the security cabinet's instructions were made public after Eisenkot issued his statement, according to Anadolu. The [Jerusalem Post reported](http://www.jpost.com/israel-election-2026/article-914671) that the cabinet had reportedly instructed the military to increase readiness for a possible strike on Iran, even though the cabinet had not met since Oct. 5. Al Jazeera quoted KAN saying the directives "could lead to military activity that could trigger a war."

Netanyahu heads a caretaker government. Anadolu reported that Israeli law does not impose specific restrictions on such a government launching military attacks, but that any attack would require approval from the security cabinet, which Netanyahu heads.

## Eisenkot's letter

In the letter, Eisenkot told Netanyahu that "only 46 lawmakers still support your continuation as prime minister," Anadolu reported. Netanyahu's office responded that the letter was "an irresponsible move and an overt attempt to politicize security issues," and said decisions taken by the caretaker government are based on security requirements.

Eisenkot questioned why his request for an operational briefing, which he said is customary, had been rejected, and why the government sought to postpone a meeting of the Knesset's Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee until next week. "I will not allow a vacuum in oversight of a government that has lost the confidence of the Knesset," he said, according to Anadolu.

Opposition circles fear Netanyahu could use a strike to declare a state of emergency and push for a unity government that includes him. Eisenkot opposes such an arrangement, Anadolu reported.

## Military caution, reported

Ynet, as cited by Anadolu and Israel Hayom, reported that Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, the military chief, and senior security officials opposed some proposals for operations against Iran.

## Iran's response

Al Jazeera reported that Iran warned of expanded retaliation if Israel acts. Rezaei wrote on social media that if the United States launches another war on Iran, "every military base involved in the aggression, from West Asia to Europe, will be a legitimate target." Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who leads Iran's negotiating team, said the "ball is now in the American court," Al Jazeera reported.

## Vance and Rezaei

The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Vance is considering a face-to-face meeting with Rezaei, the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, as the lead U.S. negotiator on Iran. Israel Hayom reported that Trump has authorized Vance to lead negotiations, with Doha under consideration as a venue. The discussions remain preliminary and no meeting is scheduled, according to a [report cited by Investing.com](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/jd-vance-takes-lead-iran-201809559.html).

Iran has said it wants an end to the U.S. blockade and the release of frozen assets before talks resume. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called those demands "totally unrealistic," Israel Hayom reported. Rezaei has denied that any negotiations are under way.

## What comes next

The security cabinet is expected to convene Sunday, Anadolu reported. Meridian will update this story if the cabinet's decisions are published or if Vance and Iranian officials confirm a meeting.
